sentences.text: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.
Access to the Secondary Inspection Chute and its associated work area is limited to personnel with authorized duties.
Explosives Response Team responds to escalated alarms and coordinates any required safety controls with airport security personnel.
In local radio traffic, Explosives Response Team is also called Pebble.
Inspection staff maintain physical control of an alarmed bag and do not return it to the sorter until an authorized disposition is recorded.
The Bag Reconciliation Station verifies that the bag presented for examination matches the screening record before further handling.
If an examination requires the bag to remain isolated, staff secure the area and notify the Baggage Operations Supervisor.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates decisions that affect flight readiness, staffing, or continued operation of a screening lane.
The Security Duty Manager is notified when an alarm response requires a security decision beyond routine screening procedures.
The Bag Tag Printer produces a Calibration Witness Tag when a calibration witness record is required.
The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is also known locally as Orchard.
The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit accepts only bags with a valid screening disposition and an authorized routing instruction.
The Transfer Bag Feeder holds transfer bags from release until their screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
Staff return a bag to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization are consistent in the operating record.
